description: A snow removal company removes snow from neighborhoods using small trucks and large trucks. A small truck requires 2 people to shovel the snow and can carry 30 units of snow. A large truck require 4 people to shovel the snow and car carry 50 units of snow. The company has available 30 people. In addition, because some neighbourhood don’t allow big trucks, at least 10 trucks must be small. There must be at least 3 large trucks as well and the number of small trucks must be twice as much as the number of large trucks. How many of each truck should be used to maximize the total amount of snow that can be transported?

PeoplePerSmallTruck.definition: Number of people required to shovel snow per small truck

PeoplePerLargeTruck.definition: Number of people required to shovel snow per large truck

SnowCapacitySmallTruck.definition: Snow carrying capacity of a small truck (in units)

SnowCapacityLargeTruck.definition: Snow carrying capacity of a large truck (in units)

TotalPeople.definition: Total number of people available for snow shoveling

MinSmallTrucks.definition: Minimum number of small trucks required

MinLargeTrucks.definition: Minimum number of large trucks required

SmallTrucksPerLargeTruck.definition: Number of small trucks per large truck

objective.description: "Maximize the total amount of snow that can be transported by the small and large trucks"

constraints.description: 2 * (number of small trucks) + 4 * (number of large trucks) <= 30
Number of small trucks = 2 * (number of large trucks)
Number of small trucks and number of large trucks must be integers
